dictionaryDefinitions.name: project-words
dictionaryDefinitions.description: This project's own vocabulary — tool names, CI/k8s nouns, author surnames, identifiers from the security-scanning skills. Kept in a plain newline file so it diffs cleanly and can be regenerated.

comment-en-GB: en-GB is loaded alongside en_US because the prose in this repo uses British spellings (behaviour, authorised, artefacts, amortised, analyser). Without it, correct English fails the build.
comment-design: design/** is the TRDD corpus. A TRDD in a terminal column is FROZEN by rule (its body must never be edited) and it quotes the user verbatim. A spell finding in a frozen document is therefore UNFIXABLE and would red the build forever, so the corpus is excluded rather than gated. This is not a suppression of a live finding — it is an acknowledgement that the corpus is immutable by design.

patterns.name: sha-pins
patterns.description: Action SHA pins. Dependabot rewrites these on every bump, so a spell-checker must never gate on them — otherwise every dependency PR fails Lint on a 40-char hex string, which is exactly what blocked PRs #21/#22/#23/#25. The (?=[0-9a-f]*[0-9]) lookahead REQUIRES at least one digit: without it the class [0-9a-f]{7,} also swallows ordinary English words built only from hex letters — 'acceded', 'defaced', 'effaced' — so a real typo among them would be silently ignored. Every realistic git SHA contains a digit; English words do not.

patterns.name: urls
patterns.description: URLs and bare hostnames — their path segments are not English.

patterns.name: example-credentials
patterns.description: DELIBERATELY-FAKE credentials in the security-teaching fixtures and docs (AKIA…, ghp_…, sk-…, AIza…). They are the sample data this plugin's own secret-scanning tests match against, so they must stay verbatim and must not be spell-gated. They are not live secrets.

patterns.name: base64-blobs
patterns.description: PEM bodies / base64 payloads in key fixtures.
